newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nycomed first half profits beat forecast.
newsitem.headline: Nycomed first half profits beat forecast.

text.p: Norwegian drugs company Nycomed ASA, which plans to merge with Britain's Amersham International Plc soon, posted first-half 1997 pre-tax profits of 604 million crowns on Thursday.
The result fell 74 million crowns short of the corresponding 1996 pre-tax profit, but it beat market expectations and Nycomed shares opened higher on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
Sales revenues fell to 3.98 billion crowns from 3.99 billion, the operating result dropped to 724 million from 772 million and net income shrank to 399 million from 448 million.
But operating revenues in the second quarter at 2.13 billion crowns were up by 289 million crowns over the first quarter and 129 million crowns higher than in the second quarter of 1996.
"The improvement in 1997 is due to higher revenues on finished products, bulk sales and contract production," Nycomed said in a statement.
It said the Focus '98 containment programme was proceeding as planned. In April-May, the diagnostic imaging Research & Development staff was reduced in Norway and the United States.
Six-month Research & Development costs dropped by 14 percent to 389 million crowns.

Nycomed, a niche player in the pharmaceutical industry, is a worldwide leader in the development of diagnostic contrast imaging agents for X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound and nuclear medicine. It also supplies a range of generic drugs and other products to primarily European markets.

Six-month operating revenues in medical imaging, the main business, fell by six percent to 2.31 billion crowns from the same year-ago period, but second-quarter operating revenues improved over the first quarter, the company said.

"Contrast media prices in the United States have been stable for the past three quarters," it said. "Two group purchasing organisations in the United States are expected to renegotiate their supply agreements for contrast media in the second half of 1997."

A dealer said: "The result was better than expected in several divisions. Imaging did very well. Things look good in the United States. Nycomed has not lost as many market shares there as you might have expected. This was a positive result and it increases the chances for the merger to come through."
Nycomed, which used to be part of combined drugs and energy company Hafslund Nycomed, announced on July 1 that it plans to merge with Amersham International, the health and technology group.

The merged company, to be called Nycomed Amersham, will create a global group, capitalised at 1.8 billion pounds, with a leading position in in-vivo diagnostic imaging agents and research-based biotechnology supply.
Conditional on shareholder and regulatory approvals, the merger is expected to be completed in late September or early October, Nycomed said.
